scope: 18 PMs with retained inputs/practices in rapid report; full canonical records preserved

BRS5-FM2-PM5.stage2a: Substrate utilisation, product concentrations, inferred production and downstream barrier/mitochondrial effects answer different propositions. Retain both Findings, including null/compartment qualifications and secondary-review classification.
BRS5-FM2-PM5.stage2b: Resistant starch and pectin retain their existing Capacity/Direct relationships to production. Preserve the historical FOS/GOS review disposition and product-only acetate/propionate/butyrate records; no ordinary-food butyrate yield is inferred.

BRS1-FM4-PM9.stage2a: PLP-dependent GAD capacity is distinct from GABA concentration, synthesis flux and the attached clinical/behavioural observations. PDXK phosphorylation and PNPO oxidation depend on the incoming B6 vitamer.
BRS1-FM4-PM9.stage2b: The existing B6 dietary route, glutamate substrate and PLP participant are all retained. Activation is a supported Derived pathway relative to GAD; no higher-intake anxiety or ADHD effect is inferred.

BRS2-FM1-PM1.stage2a: The MTR reaction, upstream folate conversion and cobalamin processing are distinct from plasma homocysteine or tumour-cell effects. Keep the human tracer and clinical limitations already attached to all six Findings.
BRS2-FM1-PM1.stage2b: Retain 5-MTHF, folate, methylcobalamin, B12 and homocysteine in their current categories. Total folate composition is not a form-specific 5-MTHF quantity; precursor and active-form records are not independent doses.

BRS3-FM2-PM5.stage2a: Chemical chain-breaking and deficient-cell oxidative challenge support a bounded vitamin E role. The existing high-dose prevention-trial harm remains an important clinical limit, not a peroxidation-rate measurement.
BRS3-FM2-PM5.stage2b: Keep vitamin E Capacity provision and its current classification. Ordinary-food occurrence is separate from formulation-specific supplementation, repletion and cancer outcomes; no high-dose recommendation is added.

BRS4-FM1-PM1.stage2a: Primary respiratory-complex structure supports metal/flavin machinery; structural cofactor presence is not a feeding experiment or a direct demonstration of reduced electron leakage. All respiratory, ROS, cybrid and Phenome Findings are retained.
BRS4-FM1-PM1.stage2b: Preserve iron, FMN, riboflavin, ubiquinone and copper records exactly as currently adjudicated. Riboflavin-derived FMN delivery is distinct from direct FMN food occurrence; missing active-form food coverage triggers research, not deletion.

BRS6-FM1-PM1.stage2a: Gastric-emptying markers, model-derived exogenous appearance and systemic glucose curves are different endpoints. All eight Findings and ten optimisation records remain, including prior nulls, formulation and status qualifications.
BRS6-FM1-PM1.stage2b: The selected fish/rice sequence and beta-glucan formulation remain protocol-specific SOP evidence. Other existing SOPs are preserved in full; none is converted into a biochemical input or silently retired.

BRS1-FM3-PM7.stage2a: Human intravenous-DHA PET estimates brain incorporation under studied conditions; neonatal-piglet carrier comparisons and MFSD2A experiments address different questions. The human PET result is not an oral food dose.
BRS1-FM3-PM7.stage2b: DHA, upstream choline and both folate/betaine KC supply records are retained. No LPC-carrier advantage is transferred to all fish, roe or oils; multiple upstream supplies do not become independent effect multipliers.

BRS1-FM2-PM6.stage2a: ChAT substrate use, choline delivery, pantothenate/acetyl-CoA provision, methyl-metabolism support and precursor compartmentation remain separately assessed. The ethanol-specific pantothenate experiment does not isolate a simple dietary deficiency or prove the proposed mediator.
BRS1-FM2-PM6.stage2b: Retain choline, phosphatidylcholine, acetyl-CoA, B5 and folate records in their accepted categories, including those not selected in the rapid manuscript. Phosphatidylcholine is a precursor route to choline, not a second independent acetylcholine effect.

BRS2-FM1-PM2.stage2a: BHMT structural chemistry is distinct from choline oxidation, tissue specificity and blood homocysteine responses. All genetic/deprivation, substrate, biomarker and Phenome limitations remain.
BRS2-FM1-PM2.stage2b: Betaine Capacity/Direct and choline Capacity/Derived are assessed relative to the BHMT reaction. Homocysteine and zinc participants are retained; an upstream conversion alone is not proof of increased brain remethylation.

BRS3-FM3-PM8.stage2a: The human n-3 exposure changed selected mediator concentrations, with important null or undetected analytes. Concentrations, biosynthetic flux, inflammatory resolution and clinical brain outcomes are not interchangeable.
BRS3-FM3-PM8.stage2b: Keep both EPA and DHA substrate relationships. Dietary composition supports precursor supply; the supplement formulation and mediator response do not establish the same response from ordinary fish or prove clinical resolution.

BRS4-FM1-PM3.stage2a: Human supplementation studies, spectroscopy, acute sleep-deprivation work, habitual-diet comparisons and pork cooking experiments remain separate evidence streams. Total creatine is not a direct ATP-buffering flux measurement.
BRS4-FM1-PM3.stage2b: Creatine and all endogenous-synthesis participants remain unchanged. Both existing preparation SOPs are retained; source-specific cooking observations are not instructions to undercook foods or evidence of a brain effect.

BRS4-FM1-PM2.stage2a: NAM salvage, nicotinic-acid synthesis, tryptophan contribution, circadian regulation, exercise NAMPT and clinical endpoints remain separate propositions. Pharmacological niacin in myopathy does not establish ordinary-food responsiveness.
BRS4-FM1-PM2.stage2b: Preserve nicotinamide, nicotinic acid and tryptophan admissions plus the existing exercise record. Form-specific chicken/chickpea assay proposals retain acid-extraction and native-free-vitamer limits; total niacin is not relabelled as either form.

BRS3-FM2-PM3.stage2a: Cellular KEAP1 engagement, nasal gene transcription after a defined sprout homogenate and the COPD capsule null retain their different systems and formulations. No gene-expression-to-clinical-benefit inference is added.
BRS3-FM2-PM3.stage2b: Sulforaphane remains the existing Regulation relationship and the sprout SOP remains. The broccoli material/preparation join concern is flagged separately; it does not remove or downgrade the PM input.

BRS3-FM2-PM4.stage2a: Superoxide/peroxide clearance, selenium repletion and infant copper/SOD responses are distinct from whole-organism net oxidative pressure. Selenium intake plateaus differ by measured selenoprotein.
BRS3-FM2-PM4.stage2b: All five participant/input records are preserved, including zinc, manganese and glutathione. Selenium and copper Capacity records retain status, population and endpoint limits; no generic intake-to-redox or brain effect is inferred.

BRS3-FM2-PM6.stage2a: A new unscored Finding adds human glutathione-reductase structure and inherited enzyme-deficiency evidence to the thiol arm of the existing mission. Chemical vitamin C–E recycling remains a separate, unchanged Finding. Curated reaction records are pathway context, not additional experimental replications.
BRS3-FM2-PM6.stage2b: Both vitamin C and E records remain unchanged. FAD-dependent machinery motivates a precursor research question only; no new riboflavin, selenium or glutathione dietary input is admitted through structural evidence alone.

BRS5-FM2-PM6.stage2a: Pure-culture intermediate formation and variable human urolithin exposure are distinct. Downstream administered-urolithin experiments do not establish food-driven mitochondrial, cognitive or ADHD effects.
BRS5-FM2-PM6.stage2b: Ellagic acid and ellagitannins retain existing Capacity and Direct/Derived metadata. Verified and provisional precursor sources are retained with product/matrix limitations; they are not direct urolithin A foods.

BRS6-FM1-PM2.stage2a: CGM variability, mean glycaemia, oxidative markers and inferred neuroendocrine consequences remain separate. The longer early-eating/calorie-restriction trial provides contrary context to a different short early/front-loaded protocol, not a reason to delete the existing SOP.
BRS6-FM1-PM2.stage2b: Both existing SOPs and both lifestyle records are preserved, with their exact statuses. No protocol is promoted to a biochemical input, universal optimal eating window or demonstrated brain intervention.

BRS-X(Circadian-FM1-PM2).stage2a: Human meal-delay effects on glucose and adipose PER2 phase differ from melatonin/cortisol phase and from a demonstrated health improvement. Animal insulin/clock experiments remain contextual and do not create extra human replications.
BRS-X(Circadian-FM1-PM2).stage2b: The existing meal-schedule SOP is retained. Peripheral clock timing is distinct from retinal light entrainment; no extra dietary substance, preferred universal meal time or clinical efficacy claim is added.

issues.concern: The shorthand says pyridoxal kinase converts dietary B6 vitamers to PLP without distinguishing PNPO-dependent oxidation of phosphorylated pyridoxine/pyridoxamine.
issues.proposal: After approval, clarify vitamer-specific phosphorylation and oxidation steps while preserving the B6 Capacity/Derived admission.

issues.concern: The phrase Directly links severe pantothenate depletion to reduced acetylcholine synthesis through acetyl-CoA provision may overstate isolated causal mediation in an ethanol-exposure model.
issues.proposal: Review whether the study isolates acetyl-CoA mediation; if approved, describe the ethanol-specific association/intervention separately from the established biochemical precursor pathway. Retain B5 admission.

issues.concern: The inherited raw preparation join differs from the described cooked/sous-vide/mustard material context. This concerns one food exposure, not the PM admission.
issues.proposal: Independently reconcile material, preparation and measurement context before interpreting that exposure. No canonical edge repair or PM downgrade in this run.

issues.concern: Direct active-FMN dietary occurrence and the supported riboflavin-derived route are distinct; current active-FMN food coverage is incomplete.
issues.proposal: Research form-specific direct delivery and preserve the existing active-form and precursor records during reconciliation; do not infer direct FMN amounts from riboflavin.

issues.concern: The retrieved GSR FAD cofactor has ChEBI CHEBI:57692, but a resolved local FAD identity and complete dietary precursor pathway have not been established in this run.
issues.proposal: Review existing aliases/identities and step-specific precursor evidence before proposing a new dietary relationship. Do not create an identity or admission automatically.
